scope: Expected UI states and safety invariants for future implementation; not a service protocol or runtime evidence.

invariants: Completion is shown only after the requested result is verified.
Rendering a fixture must never execute its request.
The queued action does not start after Stop.
No side effect occurs for an action canceled before execution.
Stop blocks subsequent actions immediately.
An active write reaches a defined safe stopping point before cancellation is reported.
The UI reports changes already made; cancellation is not rollback.
An unknown outcome is not labeled completed, failed or canceled without reconciliation.
Reconnect attaches to the existing task without dispatching a duplicate.
An uncertain operation is not automatically replayed.
Optional downloads do not block the base installation.
The desktop remains usable without an assistant provider or model.
Deferral does not claim an optional component was installed.
Invalid edits leave the previously valid revision active.
Validation errors contain no credentials or administrative grants.
No credential value is available to the fixture or rendered copy.
A locked store does not trigger a plaintext fallback.
Provider execution waits until the user resolves setup or chooses an available alternative.
An in-use disk or installation source cannot be selected for destructive writes.
No write starts while the target is rejected.
The fixture uses a display label, never a real device path.
The exact selected disk is reviewed before any destructive operation.
Cancel before writing leaves the disk unchanged.
No request is sent to an external provider.
Failure does not silently change the user's provider policy.
